rules: Validate the exact predecessor payload and live completion record before extending it; never silently strip unknown fields.
Validate the complete segment against the frozen timing schema, privacy scanner and recomputed domain-separated commitment.
Match segment case_handle to event case_id and every attempt/case-attempt/response/request index.
Match terminal kind and independently expected plan/execution/clock binding.
Derive completion-record and usage hashes from the same validated terminal payload; never trust caller-provided digests.
Accepted and mapping-unmapped events both bind record and usage; failure events contain neither.
Terminal event stores only the segment reference; the separately manifested timing artifact retains the full segment.
Legacy append API rejects v1.2 and new append API rejects pre-extended or unsupported input.
New append API requires the existing exact ledger, runtime/session/terminal write capability and unchanged transition checks.
Validate and scan before beginning the SQLite write transaction; one terminal row contains record, usage and timing reference.
Hash-chain validity alone does not prove independent consumption, actual clock capture, task completeness or current closure.
Ordinary runtime write capability is not consumed timing authority; the future timed execution gateway must supply that proof independently.
Old four-file artifacts and old A/B paths must not be interpreted as timing-enabled admission.
